articles.title: Hackers Used Meta’s AI Support Bot to Seize Instagram Accounts
articles.summary: Microsoft drops a record-breaking 200 CVEs in one Patch Tuesday because apparently they're speedrunning vulnerability disclosure. Nearly three dozen earned the 'critical' rating, which in Microsoft speak means 'please reboot your entire existence.'

articles.title: Netherlands Seizes 800 Servers, Arrests 2 for Aiding Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Hackers weaponized Meta's AI chatbot to hijack Instagram accounts including Obama's White House and Space Force accounts with pro-Iranian messages. When your AI assistant becomes an unwitting insider threat, you know we're living in the cyberpunk timeline.

articles.title: Alleged Kimwolf Botmaster ‘Dort’ Arrested, Charged in U.S. and Canada
articles.summary: CISA contractor accidentally yeeted AWS GovCloud keys and agency secrets onto public GitHub, prompting bipartisan congressional rage. Nothing says 'cybersecurity leadership' like accidentally open-sourcing your crown jewels.

articles.title: Chrome's zero-day Whac-A-Mole continues with fifth exploited bug of the year
articles.summary: Signal calls out UK's device-scanning surveillance dystopia disguised as 'child safety' measures. Because nothing protects children like destroying encryption and enabling authoritarian censorship for everyone.

articles.title: Meta to Use Off-Site Business Data for Feed and AI Personalization
articles.summary: Chrome's fifth zero-day of the year gets patched after active exploitation, netting the researcher a sweet $55K bounty. Google's Whac-A-Mole security model continues to provide steady income for bug hunters.

articles.title: Cisco Cloud Control: One Login for Human and AI Agent Operations
articles.summary: WhatsApp blocks NSO's Pegasus spyware campaign and asks courts to treat it as contempt of their injunction. Surveillance capitalism meets its match when messaging apps fight back against state-sponsored stalkerware.

articles.title: WhatsApp Catches Spyware Firm NSO Defying No-Hacking Court Order
articles.summary: Qilin ransomware gang had a month-long head start exploiting Check Point VPN zero-day before patches existed. Nothing like giving criminals a 30-day free trial of your critical infrastructure vulnerabilities.

articles.title: Can a VPN Actually Protect You From Hackers? The Answer Is Complicated
articles.summary: Meta's AI chatbot bug let hackers hijack 20,225 Instagram accounts by simply asking nicely for password resets. Social engineering meets artificial intelligence in the most painfully predictable way possible.

articles.title: Gogs patches critical zero-day enabling remote code execution
articles.summary: Former IBM cybersecurity exec whistleblows on company covering up years of Chinese state hacking. Corporate security theater meets geopolitical reality when executives choose plausible deniability over disclosure.

articles.title: Cheers to the Winners of EFF’s 18th Annual Cyberlaw Trivia Night!
articles.summary: EFF victory forces Meta to strip facial recognition code from smart glasses app after public outcry. Turns out mass surveillance is slightly less popular when people actually know it's happening.
